correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the unit-normalized Szegő Cauchy double-alternant; within-ring discrete Fourier eigenvalues yield C_m(r)C_n(s), and root-of-unity resultants yield a cross factor with g=gcd(m,n), L=lcm(m,n), a=r^L, b=s^L. Its cos(Lθ) derivative is strictly negative since (1−a²)(1−b²)>0; equality occurs uniquely cos=-1 modulo 2π/L. The exact quotient (1−αt)/(1−βt) has log derivative ≥α−β and tends to that coefficient as t→0, proving globally sharp deficit; coincident equal-radius nodes are correctly singular. The model-space Wold decomposition supports the infinite orbit interpretation but no infinite determinant is claimed. Independent numerical Gram determinants match in 72 mixed-radius cases; they are not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Full two-ring analytical algebra checked; floating-point tests are corroborative only. No claim about unrestricted two-circle layouts or smallest Gram eigenvalue.
